key_insight: Automated TIL scoring using TRIGS and a foundation-model approach (SAM-TIL) showed prognostic performance for pCR and survival in breast cancer that was similar to clinical assessment and other AI methods.
clinical_relevance: These tools could help standardize TIL evaluation for prognosis in triple negative and HER2-positive breast cancer, but they are not interchangeable with pathologist scoring.
method: Updated automated TIL pipeline to align with clinical scoring guidelines (TRIGS).
Used foundation model-based lymphocyte detection (SAM-TIL) and compared it with HoVerNet and muTILs.
Benchmarked against gold-standard clinical assessment and outcomes including pCR, overall survival, and event-free survival.
evidence_signal: In 166 TransNEO patients, TRIGS and SAM-TIL predicted pCR (OR 1.95 and 2.32), and in 285 PARTNER patients they correlated with clinical scoring at 0.59–0.69 while showing similar pCR and EFS performance to gold standard assessment.
watch_item: Because model outputs were not interchangeable with expert scoring, independent validation and careful implementation are needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Tumour region identification guided scoring (TRIGS) and foundation model-based Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocyte scoring are prognostic for pathological complete response/event free survival in the triple negative patients in the PARTNER randomized controlled trial
